latin.311:
§. III.
Acerbiorem hunc Controversias tractandi modum si facessere juberent hodieque nominati Lutherani, vel saltem Damnationes suas, Anathematismis Tridentinis haud absimiles, in Rejectiones nudas falsarum sibi ita visarum Opinionum commutarent, quibus licèt, juxta se, perituris aliquando, Autores tamen Fautoresque earum (utpote, si omnino, certè bonâ fide errantes) salvandi sint maximè & cum his Fraternitatem Spiritualem colendi,
latin.312: Reformatis cupido esset, inque unam Ecclesiam cum iisdem coalescendi apertissima judicaretur janua, utpote sub hac Conditione, cum omnibus Fundamentum Fidei Christianae, tam Practica, quàm Theoretica servantibus dextram fraternitatis Spiritualis jungere quam paratissimis.
latin.313: Factum jam tùm hujusmodi quid ab ipsis Patribus Bergensibus in Negativa Artic. XImi, quando ita scribunt: Rejicimus itaque (non autem damnamus) omnes, quos jam enumerabimus errores: (1.) Quòd Deus nolit, ut omnes homines paenitentiam agant & Evangelio credant. (2.) Quando DEus nos ad se vocat, quod non serio hoc velit, ut omnes homines ad ipsum veniant. (3.) DEum non velle, ut omnes salventur, sed quosdam, non ratione peccatorum suorum, verùm solô Dei Consilio, proposito & Voluntate ad exitium destinatos esse, ut prorsus Salutem consequi non possint. (4.) Quod non sola DEi Misericordia & Sanctissimum Christi Meritum; sed etiam in nobis ipsis aliqua Causa sit Electionis Divinae, cujus Causae ratione Deus nos ad vitam aeternam elegerit. p. m. 591.
latin.314: Ad simile quid faciendum in aliis suprà memoratis Antithesibus inducentur hodierni Doctores quàm facillimè, si recolant, omnes istas Antitheses suas similesque plures, in Scriptura S. nullibi, nec expressè, nec per Consequentiam obviam, damnatas legi; quin harum potius Antithesium Antitheses, si minus totidem verbis, certè per legitimas Consequentias, in verbo Dei asseri:
latin.315: e. g. Fidem solitariam non justificare. Jacob. II. integrô. Bona Opera ad Salutem esse necessaria. 1. Cor. VII. 19. Gal. V. 6. Hebr. XII. 14. Fidem in Christum & Spiritum S., non quovis actu peccandi utcunque quadantenus voluntario, amitti penitus. PS. LI. 13. 2. Sam. VII. 14. Corpus Christi non corporaliter unà cum Pane, idque Ore Corporis, sed Spiritualiter, & Ore fidei sumi, indeque non in Pane quaerendum, sed ex Coelo petendum esse; nec ab infidelibus, sed fidelibus tantum accipi; Joh. VI, 35. & v. 47.–59. itemque v. 63. inter se collatis. Christo, secundum Humanitatem, Omnipotentiam non competere Joh. X. Pater me (quà hominem considerato) major est; Ergo etiam respectu Potentiae: Christo autem, secundum humanam Naturam, finita omnia, infinita, vice versa, secundum Divinam Naturam, convenire, Rom. 1, 3, 4 Cap. IX, 5. 1. Pet. III, 18. C. IV, 1.
latin.316:
Faxit DEus O. M. ut sicuti Annotationibus in Protheoriam Autoris Historicam & Catallacticam Controversiarum cum Lutheranis, nunc finem impono, ita finis tandem imponatur odiis Evangelicorum mutuis, ut Historiae de his ansa omnis deinceps praescindatur, ipsi verò ad plenam perfectamque καταλλαγήν redeant, magis magisque Capiti suo Communi, Christo, conglutinandi.
TANTUM.

pass_a.311: §. III. If the Lutherans still so named would today bid this more acerbic mode of treating Controversies to depart, or at least would commute their Damnations — not unlike the Tridentine Anathematisms — into bare Rejections of opinions that seem false to them, though those opinions may, by their own account, perish sometime, yet the Authors and Favorers of them (as being, if at all, certainly erring in good faith) are maximally to be saved and Spiritual Fraternity is to be cultivated with them,
pass_a.312: there would be desire among the Reformed, and the door of coalescing into one Church with the same would be judged most open — namely under this Condition: that they are most ready to join the right hand of Spiritual fraternity with all who keep the Foundation of the Christian Faith, both Practical and Theoretical.
pass_a.313: Something of this kind was already then done by the Bergen Fathers themselves in the Negative of Article XI, when they write thus: We therefore reject (but do not damn) all the errors we shall now enumerate: (1.) That God does not will that all men do repentance and believe the Gospel. (2.) That when God calls us to Himself, He does not seriously will that all men come to Him. (3.) That God does not will that all be saved, but that some are destined to destruction not by reason of their sins but by God’s Counsel, purpose and Will alone, so that they cannot obtain Salvation at all. (4.) That not God’s Mercy alone and Christ’s most Holy Merit, but also some Cause in ourselves, is of Divine Election, by reason of which Cause God elected us to eternal life. p. m. 591.
pass_a.314: Today’s Doctors will be induced most easily to do something similar on the other Antitheses mentioned above, if they recall that all those Antitheses of theirs and many like them are nowhere read damned in Holy Scripture, neither expressly nor by ready Consequence; nay rather that the Antitheses of these Antitheses are asserted in the word of God, if not in just so many words, certainly by legitimate Consequences:
pass_a.315: e.g. That solitary Faith does not justify — James 2 entire. That Good Works are necessary to Salvation — 1 Cor. 7:19; Gal. 5:6; Heb. 12:14. That Faith in Christ and the Holy Spirit are not wholly lost by any act of sinning however partly voluntary — Ps. 51:13; 2 Sam. 7:14. That Christ’s Body is not taken corporeally together with the Bread and by the Mouth of the Body, but Spiritually and by the Mouth of faith, and thence is not to be sought in the Bread but asked from Heaven; nor received by unbelievers but by the faithful only — John 6:35 and vv. 47–59, also v. 63 compared among themselves. That Omnipotence does not belong to Christ according to the Humanity — John 10: The Father is greater than I (considered as man); Therefore also in respect of Power: but that to Christ according to the human Nature all finite things belong, and infinite things conversely according to the Divine Nature — Rom. 1:3–4; ch. 9:5; 1 Pet. 3:18; 4:1.
pass_a.316: May God Almighty grant that, as I now put an end to the Annotations on the Author’s Historical and Catallactic Protheoria of Controversies with the Lutherans, so an end may at last be put to the mutual hatreds of Evangelicals, that every handle for a History of these things may thenceforth be cut off, and that they themselves may return to a full and perfect καταλλαγή, to be glued more and more to their Common Head, Christ. TANTUM.

311: §. III. If today’s named Lutherans would drop this harsher way of handling controversies — or at least trade their damnations (not unlike Tridentine anathematisms) for bare rejections of opinions they judge false —

then even if those opinions may perish on their own view, the authors and favorers of them (erring, if at all, in good faith) are above all to be saved, and spiritual fraternity is to be kept with them.
312: The Reformed would then desire it, and the door into one church with them would be judged wide open.
The condition is simple: they stand most ready to give the right hand of spiritual fraternity to everyone who keeps the Foundation of the Christian faith — practical and theoretical alike.
313: The Bergen Fathers already did something like this in the Negative of Article XI.

They write: We therefore reject (but do not damn) all the errors we shall now list — that God does not will all to repent and believe; that His call is not serious for all; that some are doomed by bare counsel apart from their sins; that election’s cause lies partly in us, not only in God’s mercy and Christ’s merit (p. m. 591).
314: Today’s doctors would be led most easily to do the same on the other antitheses named above.
They need only recall that none of those antitheses — nor many like them — is read damned in Holy Scripture, either expressly or by ready consequence.
Rather, the antitheses of those antitheses are asserted in God’s word, if not in the same words, then by legitimate consequence.
315: For example: solitary faith does not justify (James 2 entire); good works are necessary to salvation (1 Cor. 7:19; Gal. 5:6; Heb. 12:14).
Faith in Christ and the Spirit are not wholly lost by every partly voluntary act of sin (Ps. 51:13; 2 Sam. 7:14).
Christ’s body is taken spiritually by the mouth of faith, not corporeally with the bread by the body’s mouth — sought from heaven, received by the faithful only (John 6:35, 47–59, 63).
Omnipotence does not belong to Christ according to the humanity (John 10; Rom. 1:3–4; 9:5; 1 Pet. 3:18; 4:1).
316: May Almighty God grant that, as I now end these Annotations on the Author’s Historical and Catallactic Protheoria of controversies with the Lutherans, so an end may at last be put to Evangelicals’ mutual hatreds.
Then every handle for a history of these fights may be cut off, and they may return to a full and perfect καταλλαγή — glued more and more to their common Head, Christ.
TANTUM. Stop before HEXAS Annotationum on the Prior Protestant Controversies De Coena Domini (Annotatio I).
